era_setting.place: The sloping alley beside the Hamilton Hotel in Itaewon, Yongsan-gu, Seoul, South Korea, and Itaewon-ro at the foot of it; Yongsan Police Station and the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency; the Seoul Western District Court; the National Assembly in Yeouido
era_setting.notes: The film runs from the afternoon of 29 October 2022 to the investigation still sitting in 2026, and its centre of gravity is 18:34 to 22:22 on 29 October 2022. This is a CONTEMPORARY setting, so modern stock is period-correct, and that is this episode's structural advantage -- 93.5% of the shelf is modern. What is WRONG is the COUNTRY and the LANGUAGE. OUT OF PLACE, and wrong in any cut: American or European street scenes, US number plates, EU plates, right-hand-drive traffic, Times Square, Piccadilly, Shibuya. Korea is not interchangeable with Japan or China: Japanese kana, Chinese characters used as Japanese or Chinese shopfronts, red Chinese lanterns and Tokyo neon are the same class of error as an EU number plate in a Texas film. Signage in frame must be KOREAN (hangul) or unreadable; where a generated plate carries Korean text it must be UNREADABLE rather than wrong. OUT OF REGISTER: daytime crowds of clean, well-spaced Western pedestrians standing in for a packed night alley; festival, parade, carnival, stadium and concert stock standing in for Halloween in Itaewon; drone shots of megacity skylines standing in for a 3.2-metre backstreet. The alley is NARROW, DARK, WET-LOOKING UNDER SODIUM AND LED SIGNAGE, and it SLOPES. Any clip whose geometry is a wide flat plaza is wrong for this film even if the crowd density is right. OUT OF PERIOD: pre-smartphone crowds, CRT monitors in a 2022 control room, film cameras as press equipment, COVID-era full masking as the ordinary state of the crowd (the outdoor mask mandate had been lifted and this is the first unmasked Halloween). footage_review_required is true and a labelled contact sheet must be opened by a person before any clip enters a cut.

forbidden_claims: Any victim's or survivor's name, face, likeness or personal detail. 159 people died and this film names none of them. No generated image, plate, still or thumbnail may resemble an identifiable real individual, and no archival frame containing a recognisable face of a victim, survivor or bereaved family member may be used.
Any figure for deaths, injuries, crowd size, alley width, alley length, gradient, emergency-call counts or clock times that is not in the FACTS_LEDGER with a source id.

That 160 people died. The official toll recorded by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and carried by named reporting through March 2026 is 159. The figure 160 appears in an English-language summary of a Korean forensic study reported on 22 July 2026 and is not the official toll; it may not be narrated, captioned or put on a thumbnail.

That any named official is finally guilty or finally innocent. The only judgments this production has verified are at first instance: Lee Im-jae sentenced 30 September 2024, Song Byung-ju sentenced the same day, a third Yongsan 112 officer given a suspended term the same day, Park Hee-young and three other Yongsan ward officials acquitted the same day, Kim Kwang-ho acquitted 17 October 2024. Prosecutors appealed. The appellate outcome is NOT verified -- see the ABSENCE entries in the FACTS_LEDGER. Every named person must carry their verified status, with its date and its court, inside the same sentence that names them, and no line may imply a resolution the record does not show.

That any individual pushed, shoved or started the crush. No verified finding identifies an initiating person, and the pushing, chanting and celebrity-sighting stories that circulated online are unverified.
That drugs, alcohol or a stampede caused the deaths. This was a compressive crowd failure in a confined slope; the drug claims that circulated online in 2022 are not supported by the record.
That the disaster was staged, engineered, deliberately caused, or that the death toll was falsified.

That the police did nothing. Calls were received and officers were on the ground; the film must state the specific act or omission it can source, never a blanket. A verified omission is stronger than an unverified accusation.

That closing the street, imposing one-way flow, deploying more officers or any other single measure would have prevented the deaths. No verified finding establishes counterfactual prevention, and a 'would have' is an invention.
That the Hamilton Hotel, its owner or any illegal structure caused the deaths. The narrowing of the alley is describable as geometry; causation is not established and may not be asserted.
The identity of any 112 caller, or any content of a 112 call beyond what named reporting has published.

Any characterisation of the Korean-language special investigation record, National Assembly hearing record or court judgment that rests only on an English-language secondary summary. The English summary may be cited as reporting about the record; it may not be narrated as the record.
notes: Selected 2026-08-21 on three measured gates (see episodes/_planning/EP74_itaewon_HANDOVER.v001.md): demand median 98,102 and max 3,094,297 with four channels over 100k = R-36 PASS; exactly ONE video over 20 minutes exists on the topic, at 446,612 views, and it is in Korean, so the English-language long-form slot is empty. Buildability: 2022 setting, and 93.5% of the shelf is modern stock -- the four period candidates (1911, 1987, 1988, 1989) were rejected because the shelf holds 26 clips from 1955-85. 'It could happen to you': everyone goes into crowds. Runtime band 29:00-32:00 matches EP72. script_words [4900, 5400] is DELIBERATELY ABOVE EP72's [4600, 4800] and is the one number in this spec that is not copied: EP72 measured 191.7 raw wpm on its own ACT_1 against the registry model of 171.79, an 11% error, and finished at 29:44 only because its words were sized from gen_narration_case.py --dry-run rather than from the model. Measured on EP72 itself, from the narration registry entry in scripts/gen_narration_case.py: its final dry run extracted 378 chunks and 5,276 index words, giving 1,656.4 s of speech at 191.1 wpm, a 1,782.7 s master and a 1,791.7 s film (29:52) -- so the film EP72 actually shipped needed 5,276 narration words while its own spec declared [4600, 4800]. That declared band was wrong when written, and this band is set from the measurement rather than from the model. The band is [5180, 5720], and it is DERIVED FROM runtime_seconds rather than guessed alongside it -- the first band written here, [4900, 5400], was internally inconsistent with this spec's own runtime floor and was corrected on 2026-08-21 before this file was committed or read by any tool. The arithmetic, from the v002 script's measured dry run (280 chunks / 4,669 words, a ratio of 0.05997 chunks per word): master_seconds = W/191.1*60 + (0.05997*W - 1)*0.30 + 7*1.8, and film = master + 9 s of ENDCARD, so film = 0.331961*W + 21.3. Setting film to the declared runtime floor of 1740 s gives W = 5,178; setting it to the ceiling of 1920 s gives W = 5,720. The old floor of 4,900 words produced a 1,648 s film -- 27:28, ninety-two seconds BELOW this spec's own runtime floor, which means the two declared bands could not both have been satisfied. MEASURED AND RE-DERIVED AGAIN, 2026-08-21, and this is the final band: `gen_narration_case.py --ep PD-2026-074-itaewon --measure-section ACT_1` generated 49 chunks / 734 words and ffprobed 222.025 s of speech = **198.4 raw wpm**, 186.3 words per FINISHED minute once the 48 beat gaps are counted. That is this episode's own voice at these settings, and it is 15.5% faster than the 171.79 the registry models and 3.8% faster than EP72's 191.1. Re-running the same arithmetic at 198.4 wpm with the v003 dry run's chunk ratio (312 chunks / 5,267 words = 0.059236): film = 0.32019*W + 21.3, so the runtime floor of 1740 s needs W = 5,368 and the ceiling of 1920 s needs W = 5,930. Band set to [5370, 5930]. The two earlier bands in this note, [4900, 5400] and [5180, 5720], were both derived from a borrowed rate and both put their floor BELOW this spec's own runtime floor; they are recorded here rather than deleted because the sequence is the evidence that the number came from measurement and not from a model. Word counts must be taken from gen_narration_case.py --dry-run, NEVER from check_script_length.py, which counts HTML citation comments as spoken words and over-reads by 1,000-2,200 words per script (PD_ONE_PASS_PRODUCTION_SPEC.v3 section 6.6). distinct_video_assets = 265 from the standard's formula runtime x 0.65 / 4.5 at the 1,830s midpoint. audio_layers = 4 per v3 section 0 row 4. people_plates_min = 24, above EP72's 20, because the crowd IS the subject: faces are permitted and wanted per the owner decision of 2026-08-21, and the [NEG] block must NOT contain human face, facial features, eye contact or headshot -- it must contain identifiable person, recognisable person and likeness of a real individual, which satisfies the NEG gate without erasing the people. R3: 159 real deaths, most of them people in their twenties, victims named in public reporting, and bereaved families who are alive and politically active in 2026. The crowd is the subject so faces are necessary, but every face must be plainly fictional -- distance, motion blur, partial faces at frame edge, backlight, backs of heads -- and no cut may hold one face in the alley. The crush itself is never depicted: the alley appears in exactly three states, EMPTY, ORDINARILY BUSY, and AFTER. The event is carried by sound, by the width of the walls and by the gradient of the slope. forbidden_claims is the legally load-bearing part of this spec.

revision_reason.authority: Invariant 11: generated visuals are not evidence and must not be presented as authentic records. Applied to the machine contract after 453 clips were downloaded for this episode and 20 of them carried 'ai generated' in their own archive title.

changes.arithmetic: The shelf carries 60 items whose own title says ai-generated, and 20 of them arrived in this episode's own download. It also carries 140 cartoon, 67 animation, 52 chroma and 9 greenscreen rows that no query here asks for but neighbouring words drag in. Twelve phrases are added; each is matched against the candidate's own archive title before a frame is decoded.
changes.provenance_of_the_error: These terms could not have been declared usefully before 2026-08-21, because forbidden_hit was word-wise only and a multi-word term could never fire -- 434 of 1,442 forbidden subjects across the whole catalogue were inert for that reason. The phrase matcher was fixed the same day, so a phrase now works, and these are the phrases this episode's own download proved it needs.

_forbidden_subjects_note: 2026-08-22, measured: block_ai_generated_shelf_clips flags 793 shelf clips whose TITLE says 'ai generated', and zero of them reached this pool -- that defence works. It is not the whole hole. Pixabay's ambience category ships CG and AI renders with titles that never say so: 'dark room rain loop environment ambience', 'rain sounds fireplace sounds', 'night harbor moon silhouette' (a composited moon the size of a crane). Thirteen such clips were staged here. The tokens above catch the category rather than the disclosure.
